question: According to the manual, a bus driver must have a commercial driver license if the vehicle is designed to seat how many persons, including the driver?
choice_a: More than 8
choice_b: More than 16
choice_c: More than 12
explanation: The manual states that bus drivers must have a commercial driver license if they drive a vehicle designed to seat more than 16 or more persons, including the driver.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: To get a passenger endorsement, the manual says you must pass a knowledge test on which sections of the manual?
choice_a: Sections 1 and 3 only
choice_b: Section 9 only
choice_c: Sections 2 and 4 (and Section 5 if the bus has air brakes)
explanation: The manual states that to get the passenger endorsement you must pass a knowledge test on Sections 2 and 4 of the manual, and if your bus has air brakes, you must also pass a knowledge test on Section 5.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: When should you sign the previous driver's vehicle inspection report?
choice_a: Immediately, before checking anything
choice_b: You never need to sign it
choice_c: Only if you personally repaired the defects
choice_d: Only after defects reported earlier have been certified as repaired or certified as not needing repair
explanation: The manual states you must review the inspection report made by the previous driver, and only if defects reported earlier have been certified as repaired or not needing repair should you sign the previous driver's report, certifying the defects have been fixed.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: According to the manual, when must the red emergency door light be turned on, if the bus has one?
choice_a: Only when the bus is parked
choice_b: It is never required to be used
choice_c: Only during an actual emergency evacuation
choice_d: At night or any other time you use your outside lights
explanation: The manual states that if there is a red emergency door light, it must work, and you must turn it on at night or any other time you use your outside lights. It also warns never to drive with an open emergency exit door or window.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: During a bus vehicle inspection, what does the manual say about the front wheels?
choice_a: They must be inspected only once a year
choice_b: They must be equipped with dual tires
choice_c: They must not have recapped or re-grooved tires
choice_d: They should have lower pressure than the rear tires
explanation: Among the items to check before driving a bus, the manual lists tires, specifying that front wheels must not have recapped or re-grooved tires.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: According to the manual, what must a bus have unless it is equipped with circuit breakers?
choice_a: A second horn
choice_b: A backup generator
choice_c: Spare electrical fuses
explanation: The manual states the bus must have the fire extinguisher and emergency reflectors required by law, and must also have spare electrical fuses, unless equipped with circuit breakers.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: When securing baggage and freight on a bus, the manual says you must allow riders to:
choice_a: Store carry-on baggage in the aisle if it is small enough
choice_b: Exit by any window or door in an emergency
choice_c: Rearrange baggage themselves during the trip
choice_d: Sit anywhere they choose regardless of the standee line
explanation: The manual states that baggage and freight must be secured in ways that avoid damage, allow the driver to move freely, allow riders to exit by any window or door in an emergency, and protect riders from injury if carry-ons fall or shift.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-1

question: According to the manual, hazard labels for hazardous materials are:
choice_a: Not required if the material is in small quantities
choice_b: Square, one-inch labels placed only on the driver's manifest
choice_c: Four-inch, diamond-shaped labels
explanation: The manual states there are nine different four-inch, diamond-shaped hazard labels, and drivers should watch for the diamond-shaped labels and not transport any hazardous material unless sure the rules allow it.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: Which of the following does the manual say buses must never carry?
choice_a: Explosives in the space occupied by people, except small arms ammunition
choice_b: Small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D
choice_c: Drugs carried for medical purposes
explanation: The manual lists explosives in the space occupied by people (except small arms ammunition) among the materials buses must never carry, along with labeled radioactive materials in occupied space and more than 100 pounds of solid Class 6 poisons.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: According to the manual, what is the overall limit on allowed hazardous materials a bus may carry?
choice_a: There is no weight limit as long as materials are labeled
choice_b: No more than 1,000 pounds total
choice_c: No more than 50 pounds total
choice_d: No more than 500 pounds total, and no more than 100 pounds of any one class
explanation: The manual lists among the forbidden situations carrying more than 500 pounds total of allowed hazardous materials, and no more than 100 pounds of any one class.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: According to the manual, which of the following may buses carry?
choice_a: Small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs
choice_b: Car batteries brought on board by riders
choice_c: Any hazardous material as long as it is under 50 pounds
explanation: The manual states buses may carry small-arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs, and can carry small amounts of some other hazardous materials only if the shipper cannot send them any other way. Riders may not carry on common hazards such as car batteries or gasoline.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: What is the "standee line" described in the manual?
choice_a: The line where riders wait to purchase tickets
choice_b: A line painted on the outside of the bus marking the boarding area
choice_c: A line marking where baggage must be stored
choice_d: A two-inch line on the floor (or other means) showing where standing riders cannot stand, forward of the rear of the driver's seat
explanation: The manual states no rider may stand forward of the rear of the driver's seat, and buses designed to allow standing must have a two-inch line on the floor or some other means showing riders where they cannot stand; all standing riders must stay behind this standee line.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: According to the manual, what should you announce when arriving at a destination or intermediate stop?
choice_a: Only the bus number
choice_b: The weather forecast for the next stop
choice_c: The location, reason for stopping, next departure time, and bus number
explanation: The manual states that when arriving at the destination or intermediate stops, you should announce the location, reason for stopping, next departure time, and bus number, and remind riders to take carry-ons with them if they get off.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-2

question: According to the manual, if you have a drunk or disruptive rider, where is it best to discharge them?
choice_a: You may never discharge a disruptive rider
choice_b: Only at the final destination
choice_c: At the next scheduled stop or a well-lighted area where there are other people
choice_d: Anywhere along the route as soon as possible, regardless of location
explanation: The manual states you must ensure a disruptive rider's safety as well as that of others, and should not discharge such riders where it would be unsafe for them; it may be safer at the next scheduled stop or a well-lighted area where there are other people.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: According to the manual, what does it mean if your bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve?
choice_a: You are driving too fast for the curve
choice_b: The tires are underinflated
choice_c: The bus is properly balanced for that curve
explanation: The manual states that if your bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve, you are driving too fast, and instructs drivers to reduce speed for curves since crashes on curves often result from excessive speed.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: According to the manual, how far before a railroad crossing must you stop your bus?
choice_a: Between 15 and 50 feet
choice_b: Exactly 100 feet
choice_c: Between 5 and 10 feet
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop the bus between 15 and 50 feet before railroad crossings, listen and look in both directions for trains, and open the forward door if it improves the ability to see or hear an approaching train.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

topic: Railroad Crossings You Need Not Stop At
question: According to the manual, at which of the following must you slow down and check for traffic, but are not required to stop?
choice_a: Crossings marked as "exempt" or "abandoned"
choice_b: Any crossing with more than one track
choice_c: Any crossing at night
explanation: The manual lists situations where you do not have to stop but must slow down and carefully check for other vehicles, including streetcar crossings, where a police officer or flagman is directing traffic, if a traffic signal is green, and at crossings marked as "exempt" or "abandoned."
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: According to the manual, how far before the draw of a drawbridge without a signal light or attendant must you stop?
choice_a: At least 10 feet
choice_b: At least 200 feet
choice_c: At least 50 feet
explanation: The manual states you must stop at drawbridges that do not have a signal light or traffic control attendant, stopping at least 50 feet before the draw of the bridge, and look to make sure the draw is completely closed before crossing.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: According to the manual, what must a driver for an interstate carrier complete after each shift?
choice_a: A report only if the bus traveled over 500 miles
choice_b: Nothing, unless a defect is found
choice_c: A verbal report to the next driver only
choice_d: A written inspection report for each bus driven, listing any defect that would affect safety or cause a breakdown
explanation: The manual states you must inspect your bus at the end of each shift, and if you work for an interstate carrier, you must complete a written inspection report for each bus driven, listing any defect that would affect safety or result in a breakdown; if there are no defects, the report should say so.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: According to the manual, when is it acceptable to refuel a bus in a closed building?
choice_a: Never with riders on board
choice_b: Only if the fuel tank is less than half full
choice_c: Only at night
choice_d: Anytime, as long as the engine is off
explanation: The manual states drivers should avoid fueling the bus with riders on board unless absolutely necessary, and should never refuel in a closed building with riders on board.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-3

question: According to the manual, what does a brake-door interlock system on an urban mass transit coach do, and how should it be used?
choice_a: It applies the brakes and holds the throttle at idle when the rear door is open, and should not be used in place of the parking brake
choice_b: It disables the accelerator permanently until the ignition is restarted
choice_c: It automatically shifts the bus into park when the rear door opens, replacing the need for a parking brake
choice_d: It locks the front door whenever the brakes are applied
explanation: The manual states the interlock applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle position when the rear door is open, releasing when the rear door closes, and cautions drivers not to use this safety feature in place of the parking brake.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, p. 4-4
